messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Portuguese, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Portuguese line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
Então o medo ficou um pouco acalmado, que no lago do meu coração havia durado a noite que passei tão piedosamente.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|-----------------------|----------------------|------------------------|--------| | Allor | temporal adverb “then” | **Então** | “then” | OK | | fu | copular verb “was” (passato remoto) | **ficou** | “was / became” | OK | | la | definite article (fem.) “the” | **o** | “the” (masc. article for *medo*) | OK | | paura | noun “fear” | **medo** | “fear” | OK | | un | indefinite article “a” | **um** | “a” | OK | | poco | adverb of degree “little” | **pouco** | “little” | OK | | queta* | adjective “quieted” | **acalmado** | “quieted, calmed” | OK | | che | relative pronoun “which / that” | **que** | “which / that” | OK | | nel | preposition + article “in the” | **no** | “in the” | OK | | lago | noun “lake” | **lago** | “lake” | OK | | del | preposition + article “of the” | **do** | “of the” | OK | | cor* | noun “heart” | **coração** | “heart” | OK | | m'era | pluperfect auxiliary “had been” | **havia** | “had (been)” | OK | | durata | past participle “lasted” | **durado** | “lasted” | OK | | la (line 21) | definite article “the” | **a** | “the” (fem.) | OK | | notte | noun “night” | **noite** | “night” | OK | | ch' | relative pronoun “that” | **que** | “that” | OK | | i' | pronoun “I” (subject) | *(omitted)* | “I” | **MISSING** | | passai | verb “passed” (remote past) | **passei** | “passed” | OK | | con | preposition “with” | *(omitted)* | “with” | **UNNECESSARY** | | tanta | adjective “so much” | **tão** | “so” (adverbial degree) | OK | | pieta* | noun “pity” | **piedosamente** | “pietously” (adverb) | OK | | **meu** (target‑only) | possessive adjective “my” (added for Portuguese) | — | “my” | **WRONG** (extra element not present in source) |

### Items to Review - **MISSING:** *i'* – the first‑person pronoun “I” is not expressed in the Portuguese line (subject is implicit). - **UNNECESSARY:** *con* – the preposition “with” is not required in Portuguese; the resultative meaning is conveyed by the adverb “tão”. - **WRONG:** *meu* – the possessive “my” is inserted in the Portuguese translation but does not correspond to any source word.
No grammatical agreement errors were detected in the Portuguese rendering.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Portuguese script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Portuguese text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
